Category I AIF

Venture Capital Funds

Fueling India's innovation economy through early and growth-stage investments in transformative technology and consumer businesses.

Definition & Purpose

Venture Capital Funds are Category I AIFs that invest in early-stage startups and growth-stage companies with high potential. These funds provide not just capital but also strategic guidance, network access, and operational support to portfolio companies, typically targeting sectors with scalable, technology-driven business models.

rocket_launch

Stage

Seed to Series B

monitoring

Risk Profile

Very High

payments

Min. Investment

₹1 Crore

schedule

Tenure

7–10 Years

Key Characteristics

diversity_3

Portfolio Diversification

VC funds invest in 15–30 companies accepting that many will fail. Returns are driven by a small number of "outlier" investments that deliver 10x+ returns.

arrow_forward
support_agent

Active Portfolio Support

Beyond capital, VC managers provide recruiting support, board expertise, customer introductions, and follow-on fundraising guidance to portfolio companies.

arrow_forward
trending_up

Preferential Tax Treatment

Category I AIFs enjoy pass-through taxation benefits under SEBI regulations, making them tax-efficient vehicles for sophisticated investors.

arrow_forward

The VC Journey

Phase 01

Deal Sourcing & Selection

Proprietary deal flow from accelerators, networks, and direct founder outreach. Rigorous evaluation of team, market, and technology.

Phase 02

Active Portfolio Management

Board participation, follow-on investments in winners, and active support for key milestones: product-market fit, scale, and profitability.

Phase 03

Exit & Returns

Liquidity via IPO, M&A, or secondary sales. Top-quartile VC funds target gross IRRs of 25%+ over the fund lifecycle.
